text:
Flames Nation asked this week how Aydar Suniev and Jonathan Castagna have fit after a dozen games. Our answer for Suniev: better than his ice time suggests. The 21-year-old has 4 goals and 5 points in 14 games while playing about 13 minutes a night.

His finishing is ahead of schedule (4 goals on 2.71 expected) and will cool. But the Flames are four points better in expected goal share (the quality of chances) with him on the ice than without, and Calgary has scored 5.0 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him out there. Those two balance out, which is a good sign for a rookie.

He was a 2023 third-round pick out of the Penticton Vees who went to UMass and played six NHL games last spring. He has a heavy shot (82nd percentile) and blocks shots like a veteran, 15 already. Our projection runs wide, 12 to 24 goals, because the sample is short. With Connor Zary and Brennan Othmann out, his minutes should hold. He played only 10 minutes against Anaheim, though, so watch whether Ryan Huska keeps him in the top nine.
headline: Suniev is sticking in Calgary
